syntax: kind id?(key=value,...); | kind id?(key=value,...){ statements }; block suffix ? permits either form
identifiers: [a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}; references use IDs, labels are display-only

coordinates.world: [x,y], origin top-left, x right, y down

expressions: finite numbers, constants, + - * /, sin(degrees), cos(degrees); no general code

types.variants: enum values separated by |; other types are nested constructor calls

destruction.source: world(...,damage_pool=true) enables pooled static break/topple props across linked placements and furnishing. Omitted/false retains legacy 24 reactive-object and 128 potential-fragment bounds. Pooled worlds keep at most 24 resident impact objects/128 resident potential fragments, plus 128 distinct pooled template records within existing 4096 placements and project budgets. Each template still has at most eight fragments. Template records are data, not preallocated fragment meshes.
destruction.runtime: At most 24 active fracture assemblies, 128 active debris pieces, 24 cached mesh templates and 128 cached fragment meshes. Oldest cosmetic debris yields when full; persistent damage remains for every impacted object. Intact props are streamed instances. Used template geometry is shared across active instances, unused cache evicts after ten simulation seconds or to make room. No per-cell bodies. Lamp surface pools switch off on whole-object damage and restore after repair. Damage survives streaming, R and format 7 saves; Start over resets it.
destruction.geometry: Dream 2 topple without fragment blocks compiles all parts into one stable rigid fragment. Explicit fragments must still form exactly one rigid group. Whole-object impacts may use one centered base contact, but not compound/offset contacts, foundations, seats or emitters. Existing body bounds remain unchanged; use the centered contact for a narrow pole. The root body radius remains the topple hinge envelope and must clear the visual foot. Pooled whole-object topple may retain part sway with its original GPU phase, pivots, material finishes and matching depth deformation; no spin, roll, cloth, animated joints, scattering or zone motion. Swaying topplers require static prop ownership and damage_pool=true.

components.semantics: params declares numeric formals; materials declares material formals. At most 8 unique names combined. Material formals cannot shadow numeric formals or global numeric constants. use.args and use.materials supply matching positional lists, with exact arity and types. Actual materials resolve from globals or the enclosing component material bindings. Callees see globals and their own explicit bindings, never implicit caller locals. No recursive components. Transforms, use-site identity paths and expanded budgets are unchanged.

interactionRules.selector: measure.kind; no labels, positions or random exemptions
interactionRules.scope: Entry file only. One rule per category. Applies before assembly validation to every local/imported template, placement and furnishing. Its impact replaces per-object impact for that category, or every existing zone impact for a break rule; geometry, retained structure, body, fragment groups and per-instance damage remain separate. Scene validation rejects inconsistent serialized placements. Legacy scenes retain 24 reactive objects and 128 potential fragments. world.damage_pool opts static whole-object impacts into bounded activation; see destruction. Unknown legacy categories are not inferred.

humanoid.semantics: Optional joint.bone binds a complete 12-joint humanoid on a measured decor person. Required tree: root -> spine -> shoulder -> elbow, root -> hip -> knee -> ankle, paired left/right. Rest faces +X, +Y up, left +Z; unrotated frames, root centered with positive height, hips at root height, shoulders above spine, downward knee/ankle/elbow offsets >= .5. All parts parent to bones, no independent motion/fractures. After declaring anatomy, object-root mount detail(bone=spine) adds visual parts/components in the local frame of one previously declared bone, without another joint. Mounts count toward the same 32-part budget. Engine owns speed-blended walk/run, two-bone leg poses, jump/landing and crawl/tread transitions. Existing 12-joint/depth-4/32-part and 24-live-assembly limits apply. Furnish requires pose=rest for passive rigs or motion=walk(...) for instanced ambient walkers. Ambient GPU joints preserve the full validated hierarchy without per-member CPU rigs. Collision and terrain support remain separate; no skinning, terrain foot probes or generated animation scripts.

seating.source: Object-root seat id(at=[x,y,z],approach=[x,z],heading_deg=n); 1..4 unique slots on an upright static solid prop. at is the sitting surface, not an avatar origin. The engine fits the humanoid pelvis and rigid legs; the current bench fits feet to its floor. Requires one body cylinder, without compound contacts, foundations, interiors, transport seats, moving parts, surface grounding, break zones or bouncing/toppling furniture. Whole-object break remains supported.
seating.acceptance: At most 512 world seats; sitting surface 3..9 world units above the floor; dry unobstructed authored transfer 6..40 units from approach to seat, <=4-unit steps and full 3-unit radius/17.5-unit headroom. Placement rotation and measured scale apply once. All sitting points need furniture geometry and all approaches must validate outside the furniture body; seats and approaches require 6-unit separation. No labels infer seating.
seating.runtime: F sits or stands; movement and jump first request a clear exit. One shared claim per slot, including an NPC walking to it. G uses ordinary finite carried food; working, trade, sports and boarding require standing. Broken furniture releases claims and repair restores the same slots. Seats add no physics bodies, actors or animated rigs. NPC meal.seats is an optional 1..4 unique furniture-placement list in preference order, with authored slot order within each object; complete humanoids reserve the first reachable free slot after paying, walk to its approach, eat for eat_s, release and return home. Busy/broken seats use standing meals. All claims, paths and timers persist; no queue or table service.

interiors.contacts: contact uses exactly one radius (1..64, cylinder height 1..160) or size=[width,depth] (.1..128, rectangle height .1..160); optional heading_deg only for rectangles. At most eight upright contacts without an interior, or 32 inside a static interior. Rectangles are static structures without seats, whole-object impact or route motion; circles remain compatible.
interiors.semantics: One optional object-root interior(at=[x,floor_y,z],size=[width,clear_height,depth]) with 1..4 named portal records. Requires a static solid foundation, a matching rectangle floor contact covering the complete interior with its top at floor_y, a matching ceiling contact with its bottom at floor_y + clear_height, and explicit part.cutaway roof tags. Portals use front=-Z, back=+Z, left=-X, right=+X; offset runs along X for front/back and Z for left/right. Width/height are local full dimensions. Complete scenes prove a 9-unit doorway, 20-unit headroom and unobstructed approach with steps <=4. Existing 32-part budget applies; interior assemblies have at most 32 contacts including generated stair treads. Explicit cutaway=roof|front|back|left|right keeps floor, contents and far walls opaque inside; shell tags survive instancing and streaming. The ordinary simulation supports the physical floor and ceiling. The placed object ID may be used in repair/delivery grounds without independent polygon coordinates. One enclosing volume per building, with a ground-floor support polygon for NPC work/navigation. Internal upper slabs may use explicit rectangle contacts and cutaway=above. stairs id(material=ref,at=[x,base_y,z],size=[width,rise,run],steps=n,heading_deg=0) creates one voxel volume and n matching rectangular contacts; +Z rises before heading rotation. At most two flights, 2..24 integer treads per flight, within 32 total contacts and 32 visual parts. Measured width >=9, riser <=4 and tread depth >=6 world units. Compiler checks clear supported landings and 18-unit headroom. Above-tagged static parts hide below their local lower bound, remain opaque underfoot and survive chunk transfer. Named floor id(on=building,at=[local_x,height,local_z],size=[width,depth]) binds to an existing full rectangle slab contact inside its enclosure. At most 32 floors, 20 world units headroom. Explicit static prop place(...,role=prop,floor=id) fits its complete footprint and resolves height once; no joints, controls, knockables or nested interiors. Rest, repair, social and station work grounds may name floors together with their owning building. Derived routes traverse validated generated stairs with supported elevations, at most 1024 indoor nodes and the existing combined 8192-node/32768-link/128-waypoint bounds. Only host worker packets carry graph topology. Upper furniture/actors hide below the floor inside the same building; collisions, damage, claims and saves remain physical. Lifts, upstairs commerce and separate stacked-room ownership remain missing. A room-owning lamp supplies a floor-clipped always-on surface pool; it does not light walls or occlude other objects.

stride.semantics: One cycle per length local units traveled after group/placement scale. Renderer-owned rigid rotation; no new physics or saved clock. Joint-only; explicit rest for passive furnishing; ambient instancing shares color/depth poses.

geometry.faceted: optional boolean on undeformed cylinder, cone and icosphere parts/beams; true retains flat polygonal faces as exact cut-cell contours; false preserves curved reconstruction; no new contact, grid or part budgets
geometry.outline: 3..24 simple polygon points [X,Y], 0..1 and spanning both axes; either winding, no repeated closing point, holes, touching or crossed edges; area >= .01
geometry.extrusion: outline maps across full size X/Y, centered, extruded along Z through full size Z; rotation and uniform scaling apply normally
geometry.jointRoll: roll(axis,radius) on a joint rotates all children rigidly by traveled distance / resolved radius; reduced motion rests it, prop furnishings bake the rest pose; controllable furnishings retain rolling mechanisms for bounded activation

voxels.semantics: voxels is one rigid part with grid 1..32 per axis; ordered fill/cut operations use integer half-open [from,to) cell bounds, box default or ellipsoid cell-center test. Exterior faces are greedily merged and mesh data cached. size maps the whole grid to object-local dimensions; use equal size/grid ratios for cubic cells. Optional chunks divides grid exactly into at most 8 nonempty rigid fracture pieces, only with break or a break zone; no fragment wrapper, no deform/cloth/part motion. Physics contacts remain explicit cylinders or static rectangles, not per-cell collision or arbitrary tunnels.

world.semantics: Optional world-owner policy applies after linking and furnishing. Every shaped part is an engine voxel stamp, retaining its authored envelope, material, rigid joints and fragment ownership; explicit voxels keep their exact fill/cut data. Undeformed prism/pyramid boundary cells retain exact merged planar contours, including thin shells; curved/deformed stamps use sampled continuous contours. Stamp grids use 4..32 cells per axis, fit to part dimensions with a bounded shared mesh cache; no full-world 3D array. Ground uses resident 400-unit tiles of greedy solid columns. Infrastructure uses world-aligned columns with separate surface lifts; fine paint uses .5-unit cells. Water columns retain a bounded wave field and a rigid per-column wave anchor. Resolution is fixed at construction, never changed by camera distance. Collision cylinders and smooth driving heightfields remain separate; no editable terrain, automatic damage or per-cell physics.

scenarios.semantics: Optional logical task environment, separate from driving physics and NPC clocks. Explicit bidirectional links take integer steps; source stock sells, sinks accept deliveries and cannot resell; services consume/produce one item with capacity, duration and fee. Agents have integer credits and carrying capacity. Deliver/produce objectives advance only on committed transfers/completions. Seed rotates contention priority deterministically. No generated scripts, real model calls, medical decisions or ecological realism.
scenarios.output: Step API with local observations, joint actions, rewards, termination/truncation and replayable JSONL. Prompt interpreter and agent policies are labelled mocks.

parking.source: place(...,at=[x,y],role=controllable,parked=true) or furnish(...,role=controllable); explicit solid rideable ground assembly (car, bicycle, skateboard or scooter); boats/planes keep resident controllable placements. No routes, programs, rest pose, foundations, damage, emitters, lamps, humanoid or proximity joints
parking.runtime: 256 dormant metadata/body records, separate from 24 resident route actors or controllable vehicles. Reserve one of the existing 24 live assembly slots for the occupied fleet vehicle. Static seeds and moved local poses are instanced; only the occupied vehicle has a CPU rig. Moved poses and ownership persist across chunks, recovery and format 5 saves; Start over restores seeds.

roles.ambient: bounded instanced decor motion from walk or roam, no arbitrary program, contact or boarding ownership
roles.prop: passive scenery, no route or behavior
roles.controllable: requires rideable control capability; parked until player boards
roles.npc: engine-owned route or behavior; driver-capable NPC cannot be boarded, passenger-only seats remain available

agents.legacy: omitted role infers controllable from control capability, otherwise npc from route, otherwise prop
agents.speech: state.say is 1..240 nonblank plain-text characters on idle/perform states; shown after interaction for at most 8 simulation seconds and within 80 units; does not generate speech, trade or change resources
agents.program: behavior ID is file-local; states and transition targets are local to that behavior; all states reachable from start

actions.idle: rest joints and pause route clock
actions.patrol: advance placement route and animate while moving
actions.perform: animate joints in place with route clock paused

events.interact: only radius, 10..80; one player talk press, nearest eligible NPC within 3D range; on foot and grounded only; optional familiar matches whether this NPC has already interacted with the player; optional requires checks a personal economy milestone, restricted after linking to the task receiving market actor, or the named social account actor for shared_meal milestones; optional shared_meals checks completed meals with this particular social NPC (use the commerce feature packet)

agents.execution: one transition per fixed tick, first matching declaration wins; elapsed resets on transition; per-instance clocks live outside Scene; patrol resumes without teleport; face=player turns stationary actors at 2.5 rad/s
agents.boundary: data-only bounded state machines; no scripts, pathfinding, generated input profiles or model calls; root world.player remains the original car

striking.semantics: Optional one world-owner strike(reach,speed,cooldown_s). A grounded dry standing player can hit one reachable prop in front with K, outside sports grounds. Engine checks exact contact boundaries, vertical reach and intervening solid contacts. Reuse authored bounce/break/topple thresholds and existing fragment budgets. speed is an arcade equivalent closing speed, not force or damage health. Too-sturdy props remain intact. Cooldown advances in fixed simulation time and survives R, vehicles, streaming and saves. No NPC combat, item inventory, new body, generated controller or hand tool mesh.

weather.rainDurationS: at least 10; end at least 30 seconds before cycle end
weather.semantics: Optional world-owner cycle from saved simulation time. Rain fades over five seconds, surfaces wet over ten and dry over thirty after rain. Shared ground tire acceleration/braking/lateral grip scale by wetness; ICE, water, air and indoor floors retain their existing rules. Coast stopping resistance is unchanged. Optional repair dry=true waits before dispatch for both player and NPC; committed jobs finish and keep resources. Sky and existing pooled particles show rain, reduced motion suppresses precipitation. No new clock, bodies, shadows or per-drop physics.

daylight.semantics: optional single declaration beside world/road; paused visual clock, reduced motion freezes it; R preserves clock, Start over resets it; omitted keeps static daytime
daylight.nightMaterial: optional material.night color emits after dusk; daytime base paint unchanged
daylight.lamp: object-root local position and radius 8..80, color; static prop only; whole-object damage requires world.damage_pool, knockables remain rejected. Pool switches off while broken; soft ground-projected pool, not a point light

worldLimits.layout: one world; street-only worlds omit road and checkpoints and require a spawn-connected street network; optional circuit road requires 2..64 ordered checkpoints

sports.semantics: A dry nearly level named surface connects one distinct bounce ball and two static targets. target_at/target_size use target-local units; football local +Z points outward, basketball +Z into the court. Optional sport block has exactly team home and team away, each role=npc and exactly object or objects (1..4 complete measured decor humanoid variants). team_size=2..6 includes the player on home; engine supplies the other NPCs. Optional members reuses stationary decor person NPC identities without commerce, conversation or routes; all identities count toward the existing 32 NPC cap. The member ID player is reserved for the active player. Optional roster shares the same team sizes/member lists across grounds; only the latest joined venue renders that squad and only one match plays. Engine-owned deterministic 20 Hz tactics, one ball owner, passes, catches, charged shots, tackles with cooldown and score/time results; no generated code. Football keeper defaults to NPC index 0 per side; keeper_object replaces its outfit, keeper selects its index. Optional football net_depth=6..64 matches the visible triangular side/back net in target-local Z and contains full ball spheres, leaving the mouth open. Match time, results, member poses, possession and actions persist. GPU humanoid instances preserve the CPU rig, route and ambient limits. No fouls, offside, bank-shot backboard physics or general crowd collisions.

street.geometry: open polyline in any direction; turns at most 120 degrees; bounded miter joins with square endpoint caps; non-overlapping junctions; city paving, cycle tracks and separators yield to the circuit; sidewalk strips across it become painted walkable crossings with open curbs and clear center paint; complete cycle glyph envelopes must fit a lane and clear crossings and other glyphs; optional cycle tracks
street.acceptance: every component reaches the circuit or street-only spawn with full car clearance; riding surface clear of solids; water crossings require an aligned bridge carrying the full street, cycle tracks and sidewalks between rails; dedicated paths remain separate

surface.geometry: simple polygon; declaration order overlays; cannot cover street riding surfaces
surface.walkable: optional boolean, false when omitted; true requires convex clear pieces joined to existing pedestrian pavement, dry or fully bridge-supported; no rail/runway overlap or side entry onto bridges; adds pavement for walkers and work travel, not road grip or flattening
surface.finish: paint by default, requiring color; finish=terrain forbids color and preserves the underlying terrain and cosmetic ground plants. Both retain the same bounded work coverage, furniture reservations and walking/physical validation. Terrain areas add no render mesh or map overlay

urbanGround.semantics: visual ground follows terrain/decks; streets and cycle tracks add normal road grip; explicit bridges only, no generated controllers, flattening or traffic

cityAccess.streetOnlyJunctions: nearby junctions share outer-arm crossings; short internal links have no crossing; parallel overlapping zebra envelopes share one world-aligned stripe phase

site.label: optional nonblank plain text, 1..80 characters; names the destination independently of the reused object template; no generated behavior
site.entry: object-local [X,Z], transformed with placement heading and resolved scale
site.points: world XY, entry is prepended; last point must lie inside the named sidewalk
site.serves: stop-only site references, at most 8; targets must be reachable on the pedestrian network

crossing.junction: optional true expands to zebra crossings on every connected street arm

cityAccess.junction: file-local coordinate ID; road/street use exactly one of via or points; world spawn and bridge ends accept junction IDs; includes do not export symbols
cityAccess.acceptance: static building sites require attached exterior entrances and clear dry access paths; stops must reach served sites; short overlapping street endpoints are rejected in site-authored cities

transit.stop: named route anchor with wait_s .1..30 and a site reference within 120 units; street/tram/rail require a station or stop site; walk may visit destinations
transit.semantics: street and walk add no infrastructure; tram lays rails in existing carriageways; street/tram keep complete actor contacts on accepted roads; walk keeps the body on paths/crossings/sidewalks; shuttle stops are visited in reverse on return; solid NPC rail/tram/street vehicles may use compound contacts

proportions.layoutClearance: Optional v2 body.clearance (compiled body.clearanceRadius), finite 4..128 local units and at least the collision radius, is a minimum furnishing reservation. It cannot reduce the actual visual footprint and never changes body contacts, driving, walking navigation or render culling. Omitted retains exact legacy bounds-based placement.
proportions.rule: measure sets one rest-pose extent; uniform scale preserves shape, physics and attachments. place.scale is 0.5..2 variation and must stay in the profile range. kind=custom permits deliberate fantasy sizes. Omit measure only for legacy local-unit assets.

modules.registry: host-supplied module ID to Dream 2 text; no file/URL resolution
modules.asset: imports one exported object only, under a local alias; optional control selects an engine vehicle profile on a copy with an existing seat, validated as a driver assembly. Original module/export and NPC passenger seats remain unchanged
modules.include: merges world data only; symbols remain file-local
modules.errors: module ID accompanies nested diagnostics; failure returns no partial world

population.motion: motion=walk(speed,wait_s=1) follows cached portals from accepted sidewalks, entrance paths and crossings, yielding to swept vehicles and locally spacing ambient walkers using their complete rest footprints; speed 4..24, wait_s 0..5. Requires a complete humanoid rig. motion=roam(radius,speed,alert,flee_speed,recover_s=2,gait=walk) stays dry and outside roads/grounds, flees a nearby player and recovers after separation; radius/alert 20..180, speed 2..16, flee_speed 8..60 and >= speed, recover_s .5..10, gait walk|hop. Place requires explicit role=ambient and fixed at; furnish motion creates ambient ownership, walk requires on=sidewalk. Motion excludes pose=rest, routes, programs, seats, contacts, foundations, damage, emitters, lamps, part clocks and proximity/roll joints. Validated humanoid or swing joints animate shared full geometry in color/shadow shaders. At most 192 members; fixed deterministic 20 Hz movement with render interpolation; 8192 cached pedestrian graph nodes; existing NPC, route and CPU live-rig caps unchanged. All members stay resident. Pause freezes state, R preserves it, Start over resets it; reduced motion rests poses. Ambient walkers choose bounded local passing, slowing or backing steps on accepted pavement with stable ID yielding. Existing overlapping saves separate gradually. Narrow bottlenecks may wait or back away; no general crowd physics, pushing, avoidance of decor NPC people, signal solving, general programs or ecological simulation.
population.furnish: exactly one of streets or sites; sites require count 1..12. Passive static assemblies unless explicit ambient motion; no knockables or emitters. Static break/topple templates are allowed with world.damage_pool; rest/ambient/controllable restrictions remain. pose=rest explicitly removes bone bindings and part/joint clocks while preserving geometry, rest transforms and body; it cannot disable damage, emitters, knockables or proximity joints. On place it requires explicit role=prop, fixed at and no behavior. on=sidewalk requires decor, setback=0 and no paving; the full radius must fit the outer sidewalk and leave an inner 8-unit corridor. Default on=verge stays beyond the pavement. facing=varied gives seeded headings; jitter also varies site-row spacing. Optional grounds explicitly permit named surfaces; site paving creates connected parking aprons within the 64-surface budget. Default prop furnishing cannot be boarded. role=controllable requires control capability on every template, preserves rolling mechanisms and emits parked=true; no motion, pose=rest or on=sidewalk. It shares the 256 dormant parking cap and one reserved active rig. Generated props count toward 4096 scene objects. Full linked scene reservations filter candidates deterministically. No guaranteed minimum count; inspect compiled coverage.
population.flight: decorative instanced flight, no NPC/physics ownership. Authored joints are baked at rest; wing motion uses bounded local-Z flex. All birds stay resident. Habitats must fit the world; flight clears terrain and roofs.
population.phase: place.phase_s 0..3600 only with route; shifts the entire route clock including stops. offset remains a carriage distance.

company.bounds: One optional need per existing account; initial 0..100, drain_s 0...25, below 0..95, gain 1..100; company requires a participating NPC social host/peer, or a player with an existing social host. Existing account/actor/seat/path budgets remain unchanged.
company.runtime: Simulation time lowers company at the existing 4Hz economy cadence in every control mode; pause freezes it. Completed player/NPC or NPC/NPC shared meals restore only the actual participants, once, capped at 100. Cancelled, offered, solitary or interrupted meals grant nothing. NPC hosts offer/start company activities only at or below their own threshold; priced food may be stocked in advance while an open supply counter will close before the need can be served at its next opening; player invitations remain deliberate and available at high company. Existing hunger, fullness, cooldown, consent, duties, finite food/money, round-trip and refund rules still apply. Persist company and current commitments through R, streaming and saves; Start over resets. Exact r107 migration initializes only authored company values at saved simulation time without catch-up, rewards or resource rebasing. A game need, not psychological validity, affection, dating, a general emotional model or provider policy.

companions.bounds: 1..4 unique other NPC account refs per plan; needs supply markets. One global shared social activity across invitations, player meals and resident gatherings. Hosts are stationary complete humanoids; peers may use accepted walk routes. Actual body-sized supported seat pairs and outward/return paths; upper floors require the named floor and its enclosing building in grounds, reachable validated stairs, saved supported elevations and full 3D arrival checks, existing 16-account/32-NPC/24-rig/navigation caps; 64 sparse plan/host/guest history records.
companions.runtime: NPC hosts buy missing portions through finite trade, may carry them until off duty, and reserve two portions plus both seats. Both residents finish existing commitments, walk, eat once together and return to their exact interrupted positions before decisions/program clocks resume. Cooldown/fullness and due shift/attendance margins apply. Broken seating, a 120-second blocked approach or due work cancels/refunds the donor. Pair history does not grant player meal or recipe credit. Persist journeys, clocks and history through streaming, pause, R/save; Start over resets. No new actors, bodies, generated code, general affection, dating, groups or upstairs social travel.

workGestures.coordinates: Offsets in world units (10 per metre) from the work anchor; actor-forward +X, up +Y, left +Z. X -1.25..1.25, Y .6..3, Z -3..3; left Z >= .6 and right Z <= -.6.
workGestures.keys: 2..8 ordered anonymous keys, first t=0, last t=1, gap >=.1; first/last hand positions identical within 1e-8. Smoothstep interpolation, peak hand speed <=12 world units/s. 1..8 unique programs, cycle .6..8 seconds.
workGestures.runtime: Render-only rigid arms on existing complete humanoids. Work requires a physical station; repairs use a generic forward anchor, not verified tool contact. Phase derives from saved task progress; no saved animation fields, scripts, tools, item bodies, resource changes or added rigs. Pause and reduced motion retain existing policy.

workstations.bounds: 16 stations; at is local XZ and hands local XYZ in object units, each coordinate within +/-256 (hand Y 0..256); upright static solid prop without joints; existing place.floor bindings are supported when the station names that floor and its enclosing building; dry clear 4.1-radius/18-height stand, supported hands 3..7 world units away and 6..12 high; stands separated by 10 world units
workstations.semantics: A station is one shared work claim across jobs. Work must name its object in equipment and have capacity=1. Start within two world units on foot; face the hand target without moving the body. Departure or equipment damage refunds once. Complete NPC humanoids walk there through existing bounded journeys before reserving stock/wages and return afterwards. Stationary accounts use matching ordered station grounds; commuters use their own accepted grounds. Stationary station holders accept ordinary interact transitions without handing back body/facing or advancing route/animation clocks; moving trips retain their talk guard. Floor stations require one source business and a full supported standing footprint, with connected stair/counter approaches even without assigned NPCs. Ground and upper job starts/continuation retain the same counter-radius bound; an accepted upper station replaces counter sight only for production. Purchases and business actions still require actual counter sight. Player work/bag context appears only near the same supported floor and clear sight of the bench. Work trips retain bounded elevation in pose, home, destination and path; reject unsupported heights and through-slab paths. Preserve one claim, finite escrow, refunds, R, pause, streaming and saved work. Hands are renderer-only rigid-arm targets. No item bodies, new rigs, generated controllers or offline work. See examples/upstairs-work.dream.

qualifications.bounds: 16 milestones, shared_meal task references a non-player account with social; optional peer references a different NPC account explicitly listed in that host social.peers; peer is shared_meal-only and cannot gate player conversation; requires_any has 1..4 unique milestone IDs, excludes requires; every prerequisite branch must be acyclic
qualifications.semantics: Without peer, completed shared meals qualify only the player and the named NPC account using socialHistory. With peer, only task and peer qualify, using the exact saved peerHistory key social/task/peer. Both must complete the actual meal; no reversed key, global count or stranger qualifies. Paired NPC milestones cannot gate player on.requires. Residents finish their return before taking work. Third parties never inherit another pair's history. Starting, cancelling or refunded meals do not qualify. Either listed milestone qualifies the acting worker; requires retains its single-milestone rule. Player/NPC work, commute decisions and saved active jobs share the same qualification check. Counts award no goods, wages or practice; recipes still require finite inputs, pay, capacity, hours, food, energy and equipment. Shared history cannot exceed consumed portions per good. No new saved field, free stock, general friendship or relationship score. Ordered account.works now permits five unique jobs; concurrent capacity and actor/render bounds are unchanged.

commerce.attendance: Optional account(...,commute=true,attendance=[start_hour,end_hour]) schedules one NPC workplace using its existing 1..5 work preferences, home/grounds, body and pedestrian graph. Needs daylight; opening 0..<24, closing 0..24, different endpoints; overnight and [0,24] are supported. Every assigned job uses the same market. Arrive even with full shelves or missing supplies; no input, wage, stock or job capacity is reserved while travelling or waiting. At the workplace choose an eligible shortage job at most once per simulation second through the same finite player work rules. Waiting earns no wages or practice. Finish committed work across the attendance boundary, then walk home. An affordable meal or owned food at fullness <=40, or configured low energy, returns the worker for the ordinary home food/rest routine before another attendance trip. Unaffordable meals do not stop earning a feasible wage. Existing jobs, equipment interruption/refunds, qualification, service hours, player capacity and conservation stay authoritative. One journey owns pose and pauses the NPC program; existing actor/rig/path budgets stay. Persist dutyAtS and out/idle/work/home; pin the workday to departure, never roll a delayed trip into a later day or create offline attendance. Registered old one-batch trips finish unchanged before new attendance decisions. No employee contracts, idle pay, queue or guaranteed job.
commerce.resting: Optional economy rest(energy=0..100,drain_s=0..0.25,recover_s=.1..10,below=0..95,until=5..100,seats=[furniture],on=ground,grounds=[extra]); account(...,rest=plan). At most 8 plans, 1..4 unique ordered furniture IDs, until >= below+5 and the existing convex-ground, 4096-sample, 8192-node/32768-link/128-waypoint limits. Player and non-vendor complete humanoid NPC accounts use the same bounded energy rule. NPCs may combine meal and commuting work, excluding other automatic policies. Time drains energy, work and repairs require effort before starting and spend it once on completion. Cancellation never spends effort. Player and energy-enabled NPC recovery uses any usable occupied furniture, regardless of NPC rest preferences. An NPC recovers while its existing meal or companion journey is in eat, or its rest journey is in sit; reserved approaches, standing meals and return walks still drain. Recovery stops immediately on damage or a lost claim, and never adds another journey or recovery reward. Hungry food decisions precede automatic rest. Low-energy NPCs reserve a reachable free seat, physically walk/sit/recover until target, release it and return to the paused routine. Broken or occupied furniture prevents recovery; claims share player/meal capacity. Optional shelter=true requires world weather and every listed seat fully under a retained interior ceiling with body-sized headroom. An otherwise free uncovered NPC seeks the same claimed seat when rain starts, even at high energy; energy and weather share one journey. Existing meals, work and travel finish first. Stay until rain ends and energy reaches until; a healthy outward trip can return early once rain stops. Covered healthy routines remain in place. commerce.semantics: NPC meal trips use meal id(good=food_id,markets=[first_shop,second_shop],on=home_ground,grounds=[extra_ground],eat_s=4); and account.meal=meal_id. A meal account is a measured person decor NPC with a program, optional walk route, no counter operator role, and no shop/work/repair/delivery policy. Hungry at <=40, it eats carried food first; otherwise it walks to the first stocked affordable shop with a clear outbound/return path. No reservation before arrival. The shared buy transaction rechecks stock, funds, bag and treasury. Failure returns empty-handed, without refund or pay. Success waits eat_s, consumes its owned unit once, restores fullness, then returns to the captured routine position. Program clocks pause through travel/eating/return; moving transit/player contacts can cause waits and bounded replans. Save paths, timers and ownership outside Scene. Compose works=[pack_lunch,bake], account.deliveries and meal for a finite staffed business; see examples/market-production.dream. Format 11/simulation 17 preserves registered previous worlds, all personal records and active tasks, without new money/stock or live-city graph rebasing.  Optional one economy() block per linked world. Goods, accounts, stationary-NPC markets and timed work are bounded data. One player account, one account per actor; NPC shop=true buys/eats when satiety <=40; NPC work refills to its job target and requires a stationary actor in range. The player uses explicit on-foot grounded controls. Market lots buy and sell one unit at their fixed price, with finite stock, treasury and capacity; omitted price means a work ingredient not traded. Work uses exactly input/take or a block of 1..4 ingredient(good,take) declarations with unique goods. Every input requires an existing lot, positive bounded take within that lot limit, and differs from output. Empty blocks, mixed forms, duplicate/unknown goods and fractional or excessive quantities fail. Same-good work requires make greater than its input take. Reserve max(take,make) once for that lot, subtract its held input before checking future space, and count make minus take as the completed gain. Other ingredient refunds remain reserved independently. No seed-free or no-gain self-loop. Transactions conserve credits, atomically reserve every input/wage/output room and all refund capacity, and refund every input on interrupted work. Work requires satiety >= effort; effort is spent on completion. At most 16 milestone(id,label,kind=work|delivery|repair,task,count) definitions reference existing tasks of the matching kind; count is an integer 1..1000000000, label 1..40 nonblank characters. Optional work.requires references a milestone and checks the acting account only; work prerequisite cycles are rejected. Only paid work, completed handoffs and successful repairs increment that account completion once. Start, cancel, pickup and another account do not qualify. Optional on.requires is interact-only, and can recognize player completions at that task receiving market actor (work/repair.market or delivery.to); reject unknown, absent-economy or unrelated actor requirements after linking. Milestones grant no credits, goods or controller access. Personal counters plus unassigned historical totals must equal shared completion totals. Save format 10/simulation 15 migrates only registered old worlds: old totals stay unassigned, new personal records start at zero, old active jobs earn personal credit when they finish. No guessing from truncated event history. Needs and NPC decisions use a resident 4 Hz clock, with immediate player actions/cancellation. No scripts, provider calls, offline catch-up, free replenishment or clinical/nutritional realism. State survives R, streaming and saves; Start over resets it. Collect reserves finite source cargo, destination invoice plus wage, supplier treasury headroom and both shelf capacities; sealed cargo counts toward carry capacity and cannot be traded/eaten. Complete on foot at the destination to transfer goods, pay the source business its invoice and the courier its wage once, or cancel anywhere to return all reservations. Carrying survives vehicles, R, streaming and saves. Optional account.deliveries is an ordered 1..4 unique contract list for stationary non-vendor NPCs with a connected home; it can accompany repairs, but excludes production work and player accounts. Delivery on names a convex work ground; optional grounds adds 1..7 unique convex surfaces, excluding on. The home, supplier and receiving counter need clear approaches on those grounds or accepted pedestrian pavement, with complete connected pickup, handoff and return paths. The home need not be in receiving-counter reach, so one courier can serve different destinations. All grounds share 4096 local samples. Complete-world acceptance checks pickup, handoff and return for every assigned home. Pickup and handoff approaches must be less than 4 world units above/below the vendor. NPC local food and available repairs take priority; then whole-shipment shelf demand can start a physical walking trip. Pickup intent holds one shared contract-capacity slot without reserving stock, funds or shelf room. Arrival rechecks shared player collection rules; unavailable shipments return empty-handed without goods, refund or pay. Collected cargo uses the same escrow and conservation ledger; handoff pays once, then the worker walks home. Pickup/carry/return paths and retry clocks persist, pause NPC programs and interpolate through the existing worker renderer. Live contacts block travel. Touching work grounds join through full-cylinder portals; no road or water shortcuts. No arbitrary city dispatch or scaffold.
